input.description: List files and show routes file
Search for system owner, deleteRepo, admin references

input.reason: I read src/routes.ts and src/store.ts. The deleteRepo route at src/routes.ts:26-33 has no authorization logic of its own. It passes req.params.id and req.user straight to store.deleteRepo. In Store.deleteRepo (src/store.ts:24-31), admins can delete any repo. For non-admins the DELETE uses the filter `owner = ? OR owner = 'system'`, so any authenticated non-admin can delete a repo whose owner is 'system'. I searched src/ for middleware, other callers, or tests that might add an ownership check and found none. The only other admin check in the repo is isAdminAddress, which only auditLog uses. The finding holds as written.
input.summary: Non-admins can delete system-owned repositories through the delete route

findings.text: The delete route applies no ownership check of its own and relies on `Store.deleteRepo`, whose filter lets a non-admin delete system-owned repositories.
findings.reason: The first claim is that the route has no ownership check of its own. It holds: src/routes.ts:26-33 is a try/catch around `await store.deleteRepo(req.params.id, req.user);` that returns 204 or 404, with no check on req.user or the repo owner. The second claim is that the route relies on Store.deleteRepo. It holds: authorization lives only in Store.deleteRepo (src/store.ts:24-31), which branches on ctx.isAdmin. The third claim is that the filter lets a non-admin delete system-owned repositories. It holds: the non-admin path runs `DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')`, so a row with owner 'system' matches for any user oid and gets deleted. Nothing else in src/ (no middleware, other callers, or tests) adds a guard.

evidence.code: const result = await this.db.run("DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')", [id, ctx.oid]);

input.severity_reason: This is broken access control that anyone can exploit. Any authenticated non-admin can permanently delete system-owned repository records by calling the delete route with the repo id. Nothing in the route or anywhere else in the code stops it.
